# PR #4389: Patch: dashboard-only pull requests skip the e2e smoke specs

Closes #4371

## What changed and why

Dashboard-only pull requests no longer boot the whole game stack for the six per-PR browser specs, which never serve the dashboard. The change adds `apps/admin/*` to the `e2e` off-arm in [scripts/ci-scope.sh](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4371/scripts/ci-scope.sh), keeping the `web` line on (via the existing `*) on web` catch-all) so the dashboard's typecheck, builds and unit tests still run. The one dashboard file the suite actually reads, `apps/admin/src/testids.ts` (imported by daily-only spec 49), gets a carve-out arm before the off-arm so it still turns `e2e` on. The header comment documents the exclusion in the style of the Worker exclusion.

I re-verified the reads before editing, and they held: the only code import of dashboard code in the suite is spec 49's import of `testids.ts`; `e2e/support/config.ts` mentions `apps/admin` only in a comment; nothing under `apps/web/src` names it; spec 49 is not in `SMOKE`.

## How I tested it

- `sh -n scripts/ci-scope.sh` — clean.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` — all 356 tests pass, including the new `#4371` exact-answer case, which pins: dashboard-only diff reports exactly `["full", "web"]`; a `testids.ts` diff reports exactly `["full", "web", "e2e"]`; dashboard-plus-dashboard stays `e2e` false; dashboard plus server or game-client diffs stay `e2e` true. The file's source-scan section also passes unmodified.

## Decisions and reviewer notes

- Followed the plan exactly; no departures. The only wording choice was fitting the header bullet into the existing deploy-files sentence rather than adding a new bullet, matching the Worker's one-clause style.
- Case-arm order matters: the `testids.ts` carve-out sits before the off-arm because the first matching pattern wins; moving it after would silently disable it, and the new test case guards this.
- Note for review: this PR itself still runs every job, since ci.yml scopes each PR with `main`'s copy of the script — the new scope takes effect after landing.
- No ruling note or `spec check` impact: no game-rules change.

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

# #4371: Patch: an apps/admin-only pull request skips e2e smoke
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The dev dashboard is a separate small client from the game. Today a pull request that touches only that dashboard still boots the whole game stack (release server, game client) and runs the six pull-request browser specs, none of which can reach dashboard code: the only spec that opens the dashboard runs once a day, not per pull request. After this change, a dashboard-only pull request still runs everything that checks the dashboard (typecheck, lint, its own unit tests) but skips the game browser specs it cannot affect.

## Why

- The CI scope script sends every `apps/admin/*` change to the browser specs by fallthrough, while it explicitly excuses the Worker, deploy files and lint configs for the same reason: the smoke run boots the game server directly, behind no Worker, and never serves the dashboard (only the daily dashboard spec builds and previews it).
- The only dashboard file the suite reads is that daily spec's import of the dashboard's test ids; the smoke specs and their helpers read no dashboard code, and neither does the game client.
- This is adjacent to, not covered by, the open #4219/#4362 (skipping smoke for fuzz/classifier/tool-only changes): different files, different justification, same appetite for precise scoping. A concrete past waste: the headers change that touched only the dashboard and the Worker still paid for a full smoke run.
- The dashboard's own checks are unaffected: its typecheck, builds and unit tests run inside the web jobs, which this change keeps on.

## Proposal

- Exclude `apps/admin/*` from the browser-specs scope line, with a comment in the style of the Worker exclusion, and keep one explicit carve-out so the dashboard's test-ids file (the daily dashboard spec's only dashboard read) still turns the browser specs on.
- Keep the web line on for dashboard changes, so the dashboard's typecheck, builds and unit tests still run per pull request.
- Add an exact-answer case to the scope script's holding test pinning both halves: a dashboard-only diff skips the browser specs but runs the web jobs; a test-ids diff still runs them.

## Where it lands

- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (two scope lines and a comment) and its holding test `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` (new cases; no scanned-source changes needed).
- No SPEC section (no game rules change) and no workflow files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A diff touching only dashboard files reports the browser-specs line false and the web line true.
- [ ] A diff touching the dashboard's test-ids file still reports the browser-specs line true (the daily dashboard spec reads it).
- [ ] A diff touching the dashboard plus the server or game client still runs everything it runs today.
- [ ] The scope script's holding test passes, so a future smoke spec that starts reading dashboard code fails loudly until its carve-out is added.

## Size and risks

Small: two scope lines, a comment and test cases. Risk is a skipped check that should have run; it is contained because the holding test asserts every path the suite actually reads still turns the specs on, and the web jobs (which do check the dashboard) stay on.

   This pins acceptance items 1-3: dashboard-only skips browser specs but runs web jobs; test-ids still runs them; dashboard plus server or game client still runs everything.
6. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` and `sh -n scripts/ci-scope.sh`. Note ci.yml scopes each pull request with `main`'s copy of the script (#2986), so this pull request itself still runs every job; the new scope takes effect after it lands.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, new `it("#4371 leaves e2e off for a dashboard-only diff but on for the dashboard's test ids")`: asserts `onFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx")` equals exactly `["full", "web"]`, `onFor("apps/admin/src/testids.ts")` equals exactly `["full", "web", "e2e"]`, a dashboard-plus-dashboard diff stays `e2e` false, and dashboard-plus-server / dashboard-plus-game-client diffs stay `e2e` true.
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` (the whole holding file, which also proves the scan section still passes) and `sh -n scripts/ci-scope.sh` for shell syntax.

## Done when

- [ ] A dashboard-only diff reports `e2e` false and `web` true (exact arrays above).
- [ ] A test-ids diff reports `e2e` true.
- [ ] Dashboard plus server or game-client diffs run everything they run today.
- [ ] The holding test file passes unmodified except the new case; `sh -n` is clean.
- [ ] No file outside the two listed is changed.

## Risks

- A skipped check that should have run is contained because the carve-out covers the suite's only dashboard read, the `web` jobs (which do check the dashboard) stay on, and the push to `main` still runs smoke after the merge (#3564).
- The holding test's sources-name scan excludes first-segment `apps/` paths (`NOT_NAMED`), so a future smoke spec importing a *different* dashboard file would not fail the scan; only today's exact reads are pinned by the new case. Widening the scan was rejected (it would flood with `apps/web` and `apps/edge` entries and break existing expectations).

None.

A pull request touching only `apps/admin/*` reports the `e2e` scope line `false` (skipping the per-PR browser smoke specs, which never serve the dashboard) while keeping `web` `true` (dashboard typecheck, builds, unit tests still run). The one dashboard file the suite actually reads, `apps/admin/src/testids.ts` (imported by daily-only spec 49), keeps `e2e` `true`, pinned by an exact-answer case in the scope script's holding test.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-scope.sh` | change | Header `e2e` bullet: extend the deploy-files sentence with the dashboard exclusion and test-ids carve-out. `e2e` case block: one carve-out on-arm plus `apps/admin/*` added to the Worker off-arm. |
| `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` | change | One new exact-answer `it` for #4371 after the #4219 tests (near line 533). |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, any `e2e/` spec, `crates/`, `apps/admin/` itself, `spec/` (no game-rules change, so no ruling note under CLAUDE.md rule 3 and no `spec check` impact), or the test file's source-scan section (`NOT_NAMED`, `WEB`/`E2E` roots). No spec section governs this change.

## Steps

1. Re-verify the reads (they held at plan time, the builder re-checks): run `grep -rln "apps/admin" e2e/cypress/e2e/ e2e/support/ apps/web/src` and confirm the only code import is `e2e/cypress/e2e/49-dev-dashboard.cy.ts` importing `../../../apps/admin/src/testids.ts`, that `e2e/support/config.ts` mentions `apps/admin` only in a comment, that `apps/web/src` names nothing under `apps/admin/`, and that `SMOKE` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` excludes `49`.
2. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, extend the header `e2e` bullet's deploy-files sentence (currently lines 169-171) to cover the dashboard, copying this wording: `the dev dashboard (apps/admin/: the smoke run boots jackioh-server itself and never serves it; only the daily dashboard spec builds and previews it, spec 49, whose one dashboard read is apps/admin/src/testids.ts, #4371)`.
3. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`'s `e2e` case block, add the carve-out arm `apps/admin/src/testids.ts) on e2e ;;` immediately after the `crates/engine/tests/golden/*) on e2e ;;` line (mirroring that carve-out's placement), with the comment `# The dev dashboard's test ids: the daily dashboard spec's only dashboard read (spec 49, #4371).` above it. It must sit before the off-arm: within one `case` the first matching pattern wins, so placing it after the off-arm would silently disable it.
4. In the same `case` block, append `apps/admin/*` to the Worker off-arm line, making it `crates/server/Dockerfile | wrangler.jsonc | apps/edge/* | apps/admin/* | eslint.config.js | vitest.config.ts) ;;`. Change nothing in the `web` case block: `apps/admin/*` already reaches `*) on web`, which is the required behavior.
5. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, after the `"#4219 changes only the e2e line for the tools' sources"` test, add:
   `it("#4371 leaves e2e off for a dashboard-only diff but on for the dashboard's test ids", () => { expect(onFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx")).toEqual(["full", "web"]); expect(onFor("apps/admin/src/testids.ts")).toEqual(["full", "web", "e2e"]); expect(answerFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx", "apps/admin/headers.ts").e2e).toBe(false); expect(answerFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx", "crates/server/src/main.rs").e2e).toBe(true); expect(answerFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx", "apps/web/src/main.tsx").e2e).toBe(true); });`
   This pins acceptance items 1-3: dashboard-only skips browser specs but runs web jobs; test-ids still runs them; dashboard plus server or game client still runs everything.
6. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` and `sh -n scripts/ci-scope.sh`. Note ci.yml scopes each pull request with `main`'s copy of the script (#2986), so this pull request itself still runs every job; the new scope takes effect after it lands.

- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, new `it("#4371 leaves e2e off for a dashboard-only diff but on for the dashboard's test ids")`: asserts `onFor("apps/admin/src/Dashboard.tsx")` equals exactly `["full", "web"]`, `onFor("apps/admin/src/testids.ts")` equals exactly `["full", "web", "e2e"]`, a dashboard-plus-dashboard diff stays `e2e` false, and dashboard-plus-server / dashboard-plus-game-client diffs stay `e2e` true.

- [ ] A dashboard-only diff reports `e2e` false and `web` true (exact arrays above).
- [ ] A test-ids diff reports `e2e` true.
- [ ] Dashboard plus server or game-client diffs run everything they run today.
- [ ] The holding test file passes unmodified except the new case; `sh -n` is clean.
- [ ] No file outside the two listed is changed.

None.
